cards.text: Babylon's army has Jerusalem surrounded, and Jeremiah the prophet just bought a field from his cousin. That's like buying a beach house while the hurricane's already on the porch. Now Jeremiah hands the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, and he prays to the LORD.

cards.question: Jeremiah opens his prayer with the biggest work God ever did. What does he say God made by His great power and outstretched arm?

answers.text: The seas and the dry land

cards.question: After praising God for making the heavens and the earth, Jeremiah says a few things are still too difficult for God.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah starts telling God who He is: the great and mighty God, whose name is the LORD of Hosts. Babylon's army is OUTSIDE, friend, and this man is taking his time with the praise.

cards.question: Jeremiah says God shows loving devotion to thousands, but lays the iniquity of the fathers into the laps of their ___.
Jeremiah calls God great in counsel and mighty in deed, with His eyes on all the ways of people. What are His eyes on them for?

answers.text: To reward each one by his ways
To find the ones He can trust
To keep count of every name

cards.text: Now Jeremiah walks back through history. God did signs and wonders in Egypt and brought His people out with a strong hand and an outstretched arm.

cards.question: After God brings His people out of Egypt, what does Jeremiah say God gives them?

answers.text: The land He swore to their fathers
A king to lead them into battle
A city with high stone walls

cards.text: They come in and possess the land. Promise kept. Now, friend... what do they do with it?

cards.question: Once Israel possessed the land, Jeremiah says they obeyed God's voice and walked in His law.
Because Israel didn't do what God commanded, Jeremiah says God brought all this ___ on them.

cards.text: Jeremiah points at what's happening right now. Siege ramps are up against the city, and by sword, famine and plague it has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans, the Babylonians fighting against it.

cards.question: Looking at the siege, Jeremiah tells God that what He had spoken has happened.

cards.text: After the heavens, the earth, Egypt and the siege ramps, Jeremiah comes back around to one field. Friend, that's a BIG prayer to land on a small piece of dirt.

cards.question: Even with the city handed over to the Chaldeans, Jeremiah reminds God what He said about the field. Besides buying it with silver, what did God tell him to do?

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah: “Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too difficult for Me?” Friend, He pulled a blurry old stamper out of the back of a junk drawer, so I'm gonna go ahead and say NO.

cards.question: God asks if anything is too difficult for Him. Then what does He say He's about to do with Jerusalem?

answers.text: Hand it over to the Chaldeans

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, will capture it. The Chaldeans will come in, set the city on fire and burn it.

cards.question: God says the houses that burn include the ones where people burned incense to Baal on their ___.

cards.text: God says the children of Israel and of Judah have done nothing but evil in His sight from their youth. This city has stirred up His wrath and fury from the day it was built until now.

cards.question: Jerusalem has stirred up God's wrath since the day it was built. So what does God say He will do with it?
God says the evil came from the common people, while the kings, priests and prophets stayed faithful.

cards.text: God says He taught them again and again. And still they would not listen or respond to discipline.

cards.question: God says His people have turned their ___ to Him and not their faces.
God keeps going. Where does He say His people placed their abominations and defiled it?

answers.text: In the house that bears His Name
In the courtyard of the palace
Beside the gates of the city

cards.text: In the Valley of Ben-hinnom they built high places of Baal, to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire to Molech.

cards.question: God says making their children pass through the fire was something He never commanded, and it never entered His mind.

cards.text: Now God speaks about this city of which you say, ‘It will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon by sword and famine and plague,’ and friend, listen to what He says next.

cards.question: God has named the city's fall to Babylon. What does He say He will surely do with the people He has banished?

answers.text: Gather them from all the lands
Leave them in Babylon for good

cards.text: He'll return them to this place and make them dwell in safety. After years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, nobody has to explain to ME how good that sounds.

cards.question: God promises that they will be His people, and He will be their God.
God says He will give His people one heart and one way. What will that lead them to do?

answers.text: Always fear Him for their good
Rebuild the walls of the city

cards.text: Then God says He will make an everlasting covenant with them. He will never turn away from doing good to them.

cards.question: God says He'll put His ___ in their hearts, so that they will never turn away from Him.

cards.text: And here's the part that gets me. God says He will rejoice in doing them good, and He'll faithfully plant them in this land with all His heart and all His soul.

cards.question: God says that just as He brought great disaster on this people, He will bring on them all the good He promised them.

cards.text: Then God talks about this land of which you are saying, ‘It is a desolation, without man or beast; it has been delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans.’

cards.question: In the land being called a desolation, God says ___ will be bought.

cards.text: Fields purchased with silver, deeds signed, sealed and witnessed, from the land of Benjamin to the cities of Judah. Jeremiah wasn't crazy, friend, he was EARLY!

cards.question: Fields and deeds all over the land again. Why does God say it will happen?

answers.text: He will restore them from captivity
Babylon will lose interest in the land
The people will earn the land back

findings.problem: Baruch shows up for the first time with only his father's name ("Baruch son of Neriah"). The card never says who he is, so the baker doesn't know why Jeremiah hands him the deed.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "The biggest work God ever did" is stated as fact, but the text never ranks God's works. This is not inside a joke. The phrase also steers the baker to the right answer.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card lifts "this city of which you say" straight from the verse into Papa Dorin's narration. Spoken to the baker, "you" sounds like the baker said it. The card never says whose saying this is, so the moment doesn't make sense.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card lifts "this land of which you are saying" into Papa Dorin's narration. As in stop 3 card 1, "you" reads as the baker, and the card gives no context for who is saying the land is a desolation.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
